Diogo Andrade

Hi! I am Diogo, a Machine Learning at Multiverse Computing's research group, where I am working on improving the efficiency of modern large language models. I am working hard on pushing the limits of distillation and hybrid/linear forms of attention. Specifically interested in pushing the limits of any various forms of distillation and hybrid/linear forms of attention. Lately I have also become interested in improving mid-training efficiency & quality by way of clever and improved data-mixing strategies.

Before that, I completed my PhD in mathematics at Instituto Superior Técnico, advised by John Huerta and Pedro Boavida de Brito. My research focused on higher categories, stratified bordisms, and topological field theories with defects.

Before that, I completed my master’s in pure mathematics at Instituto Superior Técnico, where I received a Diploma of Academic Excellence. I worked on string-nets and tube categories, advised by John Huerta and Roger Picken.

Before that even, I did my bachelor’s in Applied Mathematics & Computation at Instituto Superior Técnico.

Teaching & talks

2025

The bordism (∞,1)-category as a Morita category of stratified spaces

Lisbon Young Mathematicians Conference · April 2025

Abstract

Joint work in progress with David Ayala and John Francis approaches the bordism (∞,1)-category through a Morita category built from stratified spaces. Exponentiable fibrations and relative functor categories connect geometric bordisms with higher categorical structure. This perspective supplies a foundation for constructing topological quantum field theories via β-factorization homology.

Full abstract · Conference booklet
2024

A combinatorial approach to Morita categories

Hodge Club · University of Edinburgh · 15 November 2024

Abstract

A self-contained introduction to Rune Haugseng’s combinatorial construction of higher Morita categories of Eₙ-algebras and their role in topological quantum field theory. The talk introduces non-symmetric ∞-operads and explains Lurie–Dunn additivity, building the background needed to understand these higher algebraic structures.
